Res.Caption: Invoice Lines Price Adjustment (ADJ)
Res.FullDescription: It is the amount of the adjustment to the Invoice Line Price. A positive adjustment amount reduces the available concession. A negative adjustment amount increases the available concession. This adjustment would be applied where the adjustment amount is NOT applicable to all Invoice Lines on the current Invoice. Input is mandatory where VALUE BASE IS:- UT + ADJ XUT + ADJ RT + ADJ XRT + ADJ With all other VALUE BASE codes the ADJ sub-field is NOT permitted. Format is ADJ= + or - Adjustment Value Currency Code or % e.g. ADJ=-123.50 USD or ADJ=20%.

Res.Caption: Quarantine
Res.FullDescription:
If the entry requires quarantine processing for a barrier purpose. e.g. packing.
Format is AQIS=a e.g. AQIS=Y .

The Quarantine Commodity Code is a Quarantine initiative that allows for a more detailed description of the goods. Importers/brokers have the option of selecting a Commodity Code during the process of lodging an import declaration to identify the particular commodity of interest to Quarantine within a broad Customs tariff classification. Along with the tariff classification, the Commodity Code allows Quarantine to have a more detailed description of the goods therefore assisting in timely and accurate processing. Using a Commodity Code will allow improved efficiency of entry lodgement by reducing the need for users to answer a series of entry lodgement questions to identify commodities of interest to Quarantine (within tariff classifications containing goods of potential quarantine risk). NOTE: There will not be any Commodity Codes available when the ICS is implemented, but will be phased in for certain tariffs post ICS implementation. Full details regarding the Commodity Code initiative are outlined in the AQIS Import Clearance Notice to Industry 2003/04 – No 5

The Quarantine Entity Identifier is a new Quarantine field on an Import Declaration. It is optional and is an identifier of some business objects for significance within the Quarantine system. This field is currently used to identify overseas accredited fumigation parties, but may in future be used for any party registered by Quarantine. This field is optional and allows the Importer to quote additional information that may interest Quarantine. Example: Overseas Treatment Provider Number. This element is not allowed when the Line Nature Type is N30. Up to 10 Entity Identifiers may be provided on each tariff line.
Free text field used to specify the Quarantine location when the Quarantine Premise Identifier is not specified at line level
The number of a permit issued by Quarantine that authorizes the importation of certain commodities that are subject to Quarantine controls of restrictions.

Relates to food shipments. A requirement of the Quarantine IFP scheme, the producer code indicates who actually manufactured the product, not who supplied it. The broker nominates a producer code for a line of food when required by certain Quarantine profiles.

Res.FullDescription: Silver concentration

Res.Caption: Gold
Res.FullDescription: Gold concentration

Res.Caption: Copper
Res.FullDescription: Copper concentration

Res.Caption: Nickel
Res.FullDescription: Nickel concentration

Res.Caption: Lead
Res.FullDescription: Lead concentration

Res.Caption: Platinum
Res.FullDescription: Platinum concentration

Res.Caption: Tin
Res.FullDescription: Tin concentration

Res.Caption: Tungsten Oxide
Res.FullDescription: Tungsten concentration

Res.Caption: Zinc
Res.FullDescription: Zinc concentration

Res.Caption: Second Tariff Item
Res.FullDescription: The Customs Tariff will indicate when a Second Tariff item is required. This second tariff is used in the duty calculations when this is different to the tariff classification of the goods being imported.When used it overrides any duty calculated from the initial tariff classification. Format is nnnnnnnn e.g. 87149990.

Res.Caption: Security Concession Override (CON)
Res.FullDescription:
This field can be used to override the concession amount calculated by COMPILE.
Format is CON=nnnn e.g. CON=224

Res.Caption: Countervailing Security Amount (CSA)
Res.FullDescription:
Amount of countervailing security in $Australian. Calculated by the broker where provisional countervailing measures apply to the goods. The methodology for calculating CSA will be explained in the Dumping Commodities Register. CSA must be distinguished from amount of security required to be given in relation to provisional dumping measures (see DSA).
Format is CSA=nnnn e.g. CSA=6579

Res.Caption: Credit Security Code (CSC)
Res.FullDescription:
The import credit security code. This sub- field is optional.
Format is CSC=.... e.g. ICN=C23000H*CSC=ICSS

Res.Caption: Customs Receipt for Goods ID
Res.FullDescription: A Customs Receipt is issued when goods have been detained by Customs pending action by Customs or the importer, goods require payment of duty and/or GST, goods require permits or goods are prohibited and will be subject to seizure action.

Res.Caption: Countervailing Duty (CVD)
Res.FullDescription:
Countervailing Duty payable in $Australian on measures imposed before 1/1/93. Calculated by broker using a methodology described in the Dumping Commodities Register.
Format is CVD=nnnn e.g. CVD=1423

Res.Caption: Dumping Ctry/Rgn. of Export (DCX)
Res.FullDescription:
Required input where the country/region of export is different to the country/region of origin and DRC=11 is utilized. This may occur, for example, where goods have been produced or manufactured in one country/region (the country/region of origin) but have entered the commerce or trade of another country/region (the country/region of export).
Format is DCX=aaaa e.g. DCX=RKOR.

Res.Caption: Dumping Duty (DMP)
Res.FullDescription:
Dumping duty payable in $Australian on measures imposed before 1 January 1993. Calculated by broker using a methodology described in the Dumping Commodities Register.
Format is DMP=nnnn e.g. DMP=506.10.

Res.Caption: Drawback Claim ID
Res.FullDescription: The unique Drawback identification number allocated to the drawback claim.

Res.Caption: Dumping Reason Code (DRC)
Res.FullDescription:
Mandatory when entering goods that may be subject to dumping or countervailing measures. Where more than one code is valid, input lowest code number.
Format is DRC=nn e.g. DRC=11

Res.Caption: Dumping Rate of Exchange (DRE)
Res.FullDescription:
Rate of exchange used to convert DXP and ascertained export price. Used as an alternative to default rate of exchange (date of export transaction - valuation date).
Format is DRE=nnnnn e.g. DRE=0.6835.

Res.Caption: Dumping Security Amount (DSA)
Res.FullDescription:
Amount of Dumping Security in $Australian. Calculated by the broker where provisional dumping measures apply to the goods. The methodology for calculating DSA will be explained in the Dumping Commodities Register. DSA is separate to any amounts of securities required to be given in relation to provisional countervailing measures (see CSA)
Format is DSA=nnnnn e.g. DSA=7204

Res.Caption: Dumping Specification Number (DSN)
Res.FullDescription: Uniquely identifies for dumping purposes, a model, type, size or grade, etc. of goods, or a group of models, types, size or grades etc within the tariff / stat code. Format is DSN=nnnnn (up to 5 numeric digits).

Res.Caption: Duty (DTY)
Res.FullDescription:
Amount of duty payable in Australian Dollars ($). To be input when the system cannot calculate or correctly calculate duty amount. It is used if the duty amount that is automatically calculated needs to be overridden. In such cases enter the correct duty amount payable.
Format is DTY=nnnn etc e.g. DTY=456.78.

Res.Caption: Dumping Export Price (DXP)
Res.FullDescription:
The actual export price calculated by the broker using a methodology explained in the Dumping Commodity Register. Can be entered as a foreign currency amount by entering the currency code after the amount. The ICS will use the valuation date to convert to AUD or, where input, the Dumping Rate of Exchange (DRE).
Format is DXP=nnnn Currency e.g. DXP=15394 USD.

Res.Caption: Dumping Exemption Type (DXT)
Res.FullDescription:
Indicates that dumping is not applicable to either the Country/Region, Supplier or Goods
Format is DXT=a e.g. DXT=C.

Res.Caption: Effective Duty Date
Res.FullDescription: The date used for selecting duty rates and for validating fields on the declaration. The default effective duty date is export date on declaration. This will override the default duty date. Format is EFD=DDMMYY e.g. EFD=300899 (cannot be future date) .

On Declarations with a Transaction Type of “Change”, the indicator will cause a recalculation of the effective duty date. On “Nil Amendments” this is required when no other attributes are required to be changed, however the lodgement of a change effects

Res.Caption: ELAC Number (ELA)
Res.FullDescription:
When input the ELAC (Excess Local Area Content) Number enables importers to claim eligibility for SPARTECA concessions under item 68 of Sch.4 of the Tariff
Format is ELA=aaannnn,aaannnn Use comma to separate multiple numbers. e.g. ELA=AAA99999, BBB99999.
Have any goods on the declaration been imported without paying duty or excise or have they been manufactured locally.

Res.Caption: Firm Order Date
Res.FullDescription: The Firm Order date is used (concessionally) after a Tariff Concession or other instrument has been revoked but "in transit" provisions apply. To use this field the goods must be made-to-order capital equipment that is classified within Tariff Chapters 84-90. Format is: FOD=DDMMYY, e.g. FOD=300899.

Res.Caption: First Paid Under Protest Declaration ID
Res.MediumCaption: First Paid Under Protest Declaration ID
Res.FullDescription: If a series of import declarations are paid under protest for the same reason/s, this is the identifier required to nominate the first declaration ID in the series for this Protest.

Res.Caption: GST Exemption Code (GSTE)
Res.FullDescription: A code indicating that goods are exempt from the Goods and Services Tax (GST).

Res.Caption: Amber Reason Type
Res.FullDescription: Indicates to Customs which area of uncertainty applies to have selected Amber Line Processing for the Declaration. Multiple selections can be made.

Res.Caption: Related Transaction
Res.FullDescription: Indicates if a relationship exists between the Supplier and the Importer of the goods. It can be selected in the declaration at the invoice header level to default to all related invoice lines or it can be overridden on each invoice line. It can also be set in the Organization record as a default.

Res.Caption: Import Credit Number (ICN)
Res.FullDescription:
A unique identifier for the Import Credit Scheme. An importer can quote this number when they wish to offset duty amounts that would normally be payable on an importation. The ICN relates to a balance in A$ which is the total amount of credits available for offset. The import credit instrument number and security code. Balance is written off during processing. There is no restriction on the number of lines quoting the same ICN number. The ICN is input in the ADD INFO field only.
Format is ICN=annnnna/.... e.g. ICN=C23000H/ICSS.

Res.Caption: Interim Countervailing Duty (ICV)
Res.FullDescription:
Automatically calculated by COMPILE and displayed on entry print where DRC=18. Where COMPILE cannot calculate the interim duty ICV is calculated by the broker using a methodology explained in the Dumping Commodities Register and manually input as additional information. Must be entered in $Australian.
Format is ICV=nnnn e.g. ICV=8545

Res.Caption: Iterim Dumping Duty (IDP)
Res.FullDescription:
Automatically calculated by COMPILE and displayed on entry print where DRC=18. Where COMPILE cannot calculate the interim duty IDP is calculated by the broker using a methodology explained in the Dumping Commodities Register and manually input as additional information. Must be entered in $Australian.
Format is IDP=nnnn e.g. IDP=6532

Res.Caption: Instrument Number
Res.FullDescription:
If the goods are covered by an instrument type, indicate the instrument number. When quoted this number identifies the instrument which provides the means of obtaining a concessional rate of duty (from that which would normally be payable.) It is always used in conjunction with 'Instrument Type'.
Example: Tariff / Stat: 3906.90.00. 08, Treatment: 505, Treatment Instrument Type: TC, Treatment Instrument Number: 8908359.

Res.Caption: Instrument Type
Res.FullDescription: The type of Customs Instrument entered in the Instrument Code field.

Res.Caption: Instrument Security Code (ISC)
Res.FullDescription:
A unique code for instruments like quotas that are issued to an owner to use, preventing other users from finding information about the instrument.
Format is ISC=nnnn (free format) e.g. ISC=1234.

Res.Caption: Invoice Spirit Strength (ISS)
Res.FullDescription:
(Nature 30 Entries only) Mandatory field if liters of alcohol are present in QT1 / QT2 fields. It is the percentage of the volume of spirit that is alcohol. It consists of 5 numerics including the decimal point (two decimal place.)
Format is ISS=nnnn e.g. ISS=22.5.

Res.Caption: Local Content % (LCP)
Res.FullDescription: Where the CEO has determined, under a rule of origin for preferential purposes specified in Part VIII of the Customs Act 1901, that a lesser percentage of local content applies to the goods than would otherwise apply, indicate the actual level of local content for the goods.

Res.Caption: Luxury Car Tax (LCT)
Res.FullDescription:
LCT is payable in circumstances as specified in the LCT Act. Essentially it is a tax for luxury cars in addition to the GST. (LCT = 'the LCT payable') with 1 vehicle per line.
Format is LCT=nnnn e.g. LCT=1230

Res.Caption: LCT Exemptions (LCTE)
Res.FullDescription: If the goods are exempt from luxury car tax, select the code which indicates which exemption applies to the goods.

Res.Caption: Luxury Car Tax Payable Indicator (LCTI)
Res.FullDescription: Indicates if luxury car tax (LCT) is payable on the goods.The indicator is used to show the importer requires LCTI to be calculated and they will pay the amount that the system calculates. The calculation is based on one car so the quantity supplied must be one (1). Importers wishing to quote for LCTI must do so for every affected entry line using 'LCTI = Y'.

Res.Caption: LCT Quoting (LCTQ)
Res.FullDescription:
If the goods are luxury cars and the owner has been approved for deferral, indicate that the payment of luxury car tax is being deferred. It indicates the importer is quoting the Luxury Car Tax (LCT) liability for the line. This means that the payment of LCT is deferred until the last retail sale and does not have to be paid on importation on the declaration. This arrangement is intended for wholesale luxury car importers. The wholesaler must be approved by the ATO to be allowed to quote LCT.
Volume importers will be able to quote for LCT and must have an ABN. LCT quoting will not be automatic as it is for deferral of GST. Importers wishing to quote for LCT must do so for every affected entry line using 'LCTQ = Y'. This will generate a declaration for entry lodgement.

Res.Caption: Second Ministerial Determination (MD2)
Res.FullDescription:
Input to supplement concession gained through first MD. May only be used in conjunction with MD1.
Format is MD2=nnnnnn e.g. MD2=123456.

Res.Caption: Manual Line Processing (MLP)
Res.FullDescription:
This is a facility which will override normal computer calculations and can be used for complex processing cases which cannot be processed by the system. The use of MLP is restricted and an authority must be obtained from the local User Liaison representative of Imports / Exports. If authority has not been obtained, the entry cannot be finalized. Input may be continued but the entry must be put on HOLD until the authority is provided.
When authority is obtained, input MLP = xxx (authority no.). Upon acceptance the system responds with an error message which incorporates the Customs value in $Australian.
Duty must then be calculated manually and input DTY=125. Support duties must also be included in this total if applicable. Other duties must also be input manually.
Where Quota Instruments are involved, they must be presented for manual write-off and a request for balance adjustment submitted to Quota Sub-Component in Canberra. NOTE: The correct unit of quantity must be input as no conversion will occur with MLP. Format is MLP=nnna e.g. MLP=123A

Res.Caption: Manual Line Processing Indicator (MLPI)
Res.FullDescription: Indicates that the duty for the line has been manually calculated and supplied. Importers wishing to quote for MLPI must do so for every affected entry line using 'MLPI = Y'.

Res.Caption: Number Of Entry Prints
Res.FullDescription: The number of entry prints

Res.Caption: Whs. Address
Res.FullDescription: Warehouse Address

Res.Caption: Other Duty Factor (ODF)
Res.FullDescription: The value supplied on an import Declaration Line, that is multiplied by the Other Duty Factor Rate (where this is applicable) to calculate the duty for the line.

Res.Caption: Country/Region of Origin (ORG)
Res.FullDescription: Enter the Country/Region code as listed in the reference files. This is the Country/Region from which the goods in the Declaration originated. Format is ORG=aa e.g. ORG=TW.

Res.Caption: Permit Numbers
Res.FullDescription: Enter the Permit to apply to this Commercial Invoice. Use a comma , to separate permits. Example: PIL123,ABC12345. Note that Permit Numbers consist of a 3 character alphabetic Permit Issuing Authority (e.g. PIL) followed by the actual issued permit number.

Res.Caption: Preference Inquiry Number (PIQ)
Res.FullDescription:
Preference Inquiry numbers relate to decisions made by Customs concerning Preference matters.
Format is PIQ=nnnn e.g. PIQ=0123

Res.Caption: Preference Origin Ctry/Rgn. Code (POC)
Res.FullDescription: Identifies the country/region of origin for which preferential duty rates are being claimed. It may differ from the Origin Country/Region Code, as the origin of goods will not necessarily be the same as the country/region for which preference is being claimed. This will default from the Invoice Header to all related Invoice Lines or can be overridden on each invoice line.
Are the goods prescribed under sections 99(3), 102A and 117AA of the Customs Act 1901?

Res.Caption: Preference Indicator (PRF)
Res.FullDescription: Goods origin preference code. Enables preferential rates of duty.

Res.Caption: Preference Rule Type (PRT)
Res.FullDescription: The preference rule type. This is required to show the reason an import declaration is claiming a particular preference scheme and while it does not affect the duty rate it is used for risk management and to analyze the effectiveness of preference measures. It is also used to prevent a preference scheme being used to claim a lower duty rate by restricting the preference scheme to only a subset of preference rules. It will default from the Invoice Header to all related Invoice Lines or can be overridden on each invoice line.

Res.Caption: Preference Scheme Type (PST)
Res.FullDescription: Is used to give different rates of duty for a particular tariff classification/treatment code. If entered on the Invoice header it will default to all related invoice lines or it can be overridden on each invoice line.

Res.Caption: Paid Under Protest Indicator (PUP)
Res.FullDescription: Indicates that the line has been nominated by the broker/importer as being paid under protest.Importers wishing to quote for PUP must do so for every affected entry line using 'PUP = Y'.

Res.Caption: Quota Item Number (QIN)
Res.FullDescription:
The appropriate quota item number to be used with a Quota affected Tariff classification, as issued by the Industry Assistance Sub- Program in Canberra.
Format is QIN=nna e.g. QIN=21V

Res.Caption: Tariff Quota Security Code (QSC)
Res.FullDescription:
The quota security code number. This sub-field is only required when a Tariff Quota Number is quoted in the "Instrument No" field on the line.
Format is QSC=..... e.g. QSC=QWN1

Res.Caption: Second Quantity (QT2)
Res.FullDescription: Second quantity is indicated in the Customs Tariff if required. Format is QT2=nnnn e.g. QT2=400.

Res.Caption: Related Transaction
Res.FullDescription: Indicates if a relationship exists between the Supplier of the Goods and the Importer. It can be selected at the invoice header level to default to all related invoice lines or can be selected on each invoice line as an override. It can also be set in the product files as a default value.

Res.Caption: Rate Number (RNO)
Res.FullDescription: Tariff Rate Numbers are specified in the Customs Tariff id required. These rate numbers are used to identify the duty rate applicable in some tariff sub headings which have multiple duty rates. Generally there is only one rate value used 'RNO=001' but other tariff rate numbers may be applied where the tariff indicates their use.

Res.Caption: Security Number (SCN)
Res.FullDescription: If the goods are subject to an end-use condition, dumping or countervailing provisional measures or are temporary importations, indicate the number allocated by Customs to the security which relates to the goods. Format is SCN=xxxxxxxxx (9 alpha characters).

Res.Caption: Security Calculate Indicator
Res.FullDescription: Indicate here if the amount of security for the goods is required to be calculated by Customs. If the indicator is sent on a pre-lodgement for an Import Declaration it ensures the response message from Customs includes the calculated amount of security required. This enables the Importer/Broker to arrange for the security before lodging the Import Declaration and ensures the Security amount is correct and will match when the import declaration message is sent to Customs. Importers wishing to quote for SEC must do so for every affected entry line using \'SEC = Y\'.

Res.Caption: Standard Duty (STD)
Res.FullDescription: If the standard amount of duty, as automatically calculated, needs to be overridden, enter the correct amount of standard duty payable.Standard duty is calculated where goods are entered with a Tariff Concession Order or security. It is expressed in Australian Dollars ($). It is the amount of duty that would otherwise be payable and from which is deducted the amount of duty actually paid to arrive at the amount of concession. The amount of concession is recorded for statistical purposes. Format is STD=nnnn e.g. STD=234.56.

Res.Caption: Tariff Advice Number (TAN)
Res.FullDescription:
The reference number relating to a decision made by Customs regarding the tariff classification of goods. When cited on the Import Declaration, this number indicates that the decision on the TAN applies to the goods being imported.
Format is TAN=nnnnnnn e.g. TAN=1234567.

Res.Caption: Second Tariff Concession Order (TC2)
Res.FullDescription:
Input to supplement concession gained through first TCO. May only be used in conjunction with TC1.
Format is TC2=nnnnnnn e.g. TC2=8840003.

Res.Caption: Tariff Quota Number (TFQ)
Res.FullDescription:
Number of tariff quota instrument and security code. Balance is written off during processing. There is no restriction on the number of lines quoting the same TFQ number.
Format is TFQ=nnn (free format) e.g. TFQ=W1234/QW1

Res.Caption: T & I Override (TILV)
Res.FullDescription: The value you enter here will override transport and insurance cost in line. Enter amount + three-letter Currency code. If you don't enter a currency, the amount is assumed as in AUD.

Res.Caption: Second Treatment
Res.FullDescription: When quoted in this number identifies the instrument which provides the means of obtaining a concessional rate of duty (from that which would normally be payable). It is always used in conjunction with "Instrument Type".

Res.Caption: Treatment Code
Res.FullDescription: A means by which normal rates of duty may be modified according to the Customs Tariff. This code, allocated in conjunction with the ABS, is for the concessional item in Schedule 4 or Supplementary Provisions that goods are entered under.

Res.Caption: Treatment Rate Number (TRN)
Res.FullDescription: Used to nominate a specific Rate for the Treatment Code. Treatment Codes may have more than one Rate for different reasons. Generally there is only one value, (e.g.; RNO = 001) however other Treatment Code Rate Numbers can be used when required.

Res.Caption: Unaccompanied Personal Effects Dec. ID
Res.FullDescription: The ID Number of a Customs Unaccompanied Personal Effects Document which represents a declaration to Customs by a Party concerning Goods that may cross the border.

Res.Caption: Unit of Second Quantity (UQ2)
Res.FullDescription: Second Unit of Quantity is indicated in the Customs Tariff if required. Enter the Unit of Quantity in which the second quantity is expressed. This field is Mandatory wherever a second quantity is input. Format is UQ2=aa e.g. UQ2=kg.

Res.Caption: Valuation Basis
Res.FullDescription: Select the Valuation Basis Type used to determine the Customs Value on this Commercial Invoice. Valuation Basis Types are specific to the Valuation methods used in International Trade when determining the Customs Value of goods. It may be entered in the Declaration on the Invoice Header level to default to all related invoice lines or can be overridden on each invoice line. It can also be set in the Organization records as a default.

Res.Caption: Valuation Basis
Res.FullDescription: Code used to indicate the basis from which the Customs Value is derived

Res.Caption: Valuation Advice Number (VAN)
Res.FullDescription: Unique identifying number allocated to the Valuation Advice, generated by the TAPIN system. Valuation advices are provided on request from Government Customs.

Res.Caption: Vehicle Registration Numbers
Res.FullDescription:
The unique identification number allocated by the vehicle manufacturer to each motor vehicle they produce.
Format is VID=an35, an35 e.g. VID=aaaaaaaaaa1234567890bbbbbbbbbb12345, 1234567890aaaaaaaaaa1234567890bbbbb.
Indicates that a Visual Examination Application has been lodged for the consignment specified on the Declaration.

Res.Caption: Wine Equalization Tax (WET)
Res.FullDescription: WET will be payable for WET goods unless an importer can quote or claim an exemption.

Res.Caption: WET Exemptions (WETE)
Res.FullDescription: The type of wine equalization tax (WET) exemption applicable to the goods.

Res.Caption: Wet Quoting (WETQ)
Res.FullDescription:
If the goods are wines and the owner has been approved for deferral, indicate if the payment of wine equalization tax is being deferred. It indicates the importer is quoting the wine equalization tax (WET) liability for the line. This means that the payment of WET is deferred until the last retail sale and does not have to be paid on the declaration. This arrangement is intended for high volume wine importers. The importer must be approved by the ATO to quote WET.
Some importers will be entitled to quote for WET and must have an ABN. WET quoting will not be automatic as it is for deferral of GST. Importers wish to quote for WET must do so for every affected entry line using 'WETQ = Y'. This will generate a declaration for entry lodgement.

Res.Caption: Multiple Clearance Code (WMC)
Res.FullDescription: A customs allocated number used for ex-warehousing entries that refers to multiple warehousing entries. This element is only allowed when the Line Nature Type is N30. Multiple Clearance Code and Warehouse Reference No (Declaration Identifier) are not allowed together.

Res.Caption: Warehouse Reference Line (WRL)
Res.FullDescription: Warehouse Reference Line (Identifies the line of the nature 20 entry). Where a Warehouse Reference Line Number is supplied a Warehouse Reference No (Declaration Identifier) must also be supplied. This element is only allowed when the Line Nature Type is N30. The supplied line number must exist for the Warehousing Declaration (Line Nature Type equals N20) and must not be deleted.

Res.Caption: Warehouse Reference Number (WRN)
Res.FullDescription:
On a Nature 30 Import Declaration, it is the ICS (or Compile) Nature 20 Warehousing Declaration Number that the goods were originally imported on. Multiple Clearance Code and Warehouse reference No (Declaration Identifier) are not allowed together. This element is only allowed when the Line Nature Type is N30. Additionally the line number from the Warehousing Declaration (Warehouse Related Line, Line Nature Type equals N20) that relates to the goods in the ex Warehousing Declaration (Line Nature Type equals N30) must be supplied.
.

Res.Caption: Warehouse Reference Quantity (WRQ)
Res.FullDescription:
(Nature 20 Entries only) Optional field and relates to the quantity most commonly used for recording purposes in the warehouse. It can accommodate up to eleven characters including the decimal point (two decimal places).
Format is WRQ=nnnn e.g. WRQ=328.4.

Res.Caption: Warehouse Reference Unit of Quantity (WRU)
Res.FullDescription:
(Nature 20 Entries only) Optional field and relates to WRQ. It can contain any two character Unit of Quantity Code. Appendix E has a full list of valid quantity codes.
Format is aa or an e.g. WRU=KG or M3
Note: If WRU is input, WRQ must be present.

Res.Caption: Warehouse Unit Value (WUV)
Res.FullDescription:
(Nature 20 Entries only) Consists of eight whole and four decimal numerics. Optional field and normally relates to the Warehouse Reference Quantity.
Format is WUV=nnnn e.g. WUV=340.2590 Note: If not input and WRQ and WRU are present the value is determined by dividing WRQ into Customs Value. If WRU and WRQ are not input, it is calculated by dividing the first line quantity into the line Customs Value.

Res.Caption: Warehouse Establishment Code
Res.FullDescription: For Tobacco only, when on-sold and claiming for a refund. N10 and N30 only.
